# BLO-42185 — teardown pod reaper: an unparseable pod list is not zero pods

Change: [BLO-42185](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/BLO/issues/BLO-42185),
follow-up to [BLO-35486](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/BLO/issues/BLO-35486)
(#2336).

Changed files:

- `src/server/execute.ts` — `deleteJobPodsAndWait` read
  `podList?.items ?? []`, so a list response with no `items` array produced
  `lastObserved === 0` and the `gone` verdict, which is what licenses
  `deleteRunSecrets`. It now requires `Array.isArray(podList.items)` and
  otherwise throws into the existing "could not observe" catch, which retries to
  the deadline and fails closed into `unobserved` (or `alive`/`undeleted` when an
  earlier poll saw pods). The thrown message is not 404-shaped, so `isK8s404`
  cannot turn it back into `gone`. The other two `listNamespacedPod` callers use
  `podList.items` bare and already throw on a missing array.
- `src/server/execute.test.ts` — a test that an `items`-less list never deletes
  the run Secret or the Job, and a control that a list genuinely returning zero
  pods still reaps it. The `execute: job creation` block now arms
  `mockCoreListPods` with an unschedulable owned pod through
  `armJobCreationDefaults()`, which its beforeEach calls; 12 of its tests had
  been passing on the fail-open itself.

Why: an unparseable read was treated as positive evidence that no pod could
still mount the credential-bearing `ac-<run>-env` Secret, so the Secret could be
deleted under a live pod — the BLO-35486 failure by a second route.

No upstream change: the BLO-35486 teardown reaper is Blockcast-local code in the
vendored adapter, not a carried patch against an upstream adapter release.
